source_text: 1. Quia ergo post primas illas dissertiones, quas de patre et filio et spiritu sancto in initiis seeundum quod res poposcerat exposuimus, visum est rursum repetere nos debere et ostendere quod deus idem esset creator et conditor mundi et pater domini nostri lesu Christi, id est legis et prophetarum atque evangeliorum unus atque idem deus, tum deinde etiam de Christo, quod is, qui verbum et sapientia dei superius fuerat ostensus, etiam qualiter homo factus est in consequentibus debuit demonstrari: superest ut etiam de spiritu sancto quam possumus breviter repetamus. j Tempus est ergo nunc de spiritu saneto nos pro viribus pauca disserere, quem dominus et salvator noster in evangelio secundum lohannem ‘paracletum’ nominavit. Sicut enim idem ipse deus atque idem ipse Christus, ita idem ipse et spiritus sanctus est, qui et in prophetis et in apostolis fuit, id est sive in illis, qui ante adventum Christi deo crediderunt, sive in his, qui per Christum confugerunt ad deum. Et duos quidem deos ausos esse haereticos dicere et duos Christos audivimus, duos autem spiritus sanctos numquam cognovimus ab aliquo praedicari. Quomodo enim hoc de scripturis poterunt affirmare, aut quam differentiam dare poterunt inter spiritum sanctum et spiritum sanctum? si tamen definitio aliqua aut descriptio inveniri potest spiritus saneti. Nam ut concedamus Marcioni vel Valentino posse differentias deitatis inducere et aliam boni naturam aliam vero 1usti describere, quid excogitabit aut quid inveniet, ut differentiam sancti spiritus introdueat? Nihil ergo illos posse ad indicium qualiscumque differentiae arbitror invenire. 2. Nos vero aestimamus quod participationem eius similiter ut sapientiae dei et verbi dei absque ulla differentia creatura rationabilis omnis assumat. Video tamen quod praecipuus spiritus sancti adventus ad homines post ascensionem Christi in caelos magis quam ante adventum elus declaretur. Antea namque solis prophetis et paucis, si qui forte in populo meruisset, donum sancti spiritus praebebatur; post adventum vero salvatoris scriptum est ‘adimpletum esse illud, quod dietum fuerat in propheta lohele quia “erit in novissimis diebus, et effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem, et prophetabunt”; quod utique tale est sicut illud, quod ait: “Omnes gentes servient eic. Per : gratiam ergo saneti spiritus cum reliquis quam plurimis etiam illud magnificentissimum demonstratur, quod ea, quae in prophetis seripta sunt vel in lege Moysi, pauci tune. x, id est ipsi prophetae et vix sicubi unus ex omni populo superare poterat intellectum corporeum et maius aliquid. sentire, id est spiritale quid poterat intellegere in lege vel prophetis; nune autem innumerae sunt multitudines credentium, qui lice& non omnes possint per ordinem atque ad liquidum spiritalis intellegentiae explanare consequentiam, tamen omnes paene persuasum habent quod neque circumcisio corporaliter intellegi debeat neque otium sabbati vel sanguinis effusio pecoris, neque quod de his Moysi responsa darentur a deo: qui utique sensus dubium non est quod spiritus sancti virtute omnibus suggeratur. 3. Sicut. autem multi sunt intellectus de Christo, qui utique quamvis "saplentia- sit, non tamen in omnibus sapientiae agit aut obtinet vim nisi in his, qui in ipso sapientiae student (neque cum -medicus- dicatur, erga omnes quasi medicus agit, sed erga illos tantum, qui aegritudinis suae intellecto languore confugiunt ad misericordiam eius, ut possint consequi sanitatem): ita arbitror etiam de spiritu sancto, in quo omnis est natura donorum. ‘Aliis’ namque praebetur ‘per spiritum sermo sapientiae, alüs sermo scientiae, alüs fides’; et ita per singulos, qui eum capere possunt, hoc efficitur vel hoc intellegitur ipse spiritus, quo indiget ille, qui eum participare meruerit. Quas divisiones ac differentias non advertentes hi, qui “paracletum- eum in evangelio audiunt nominari, neque considerantes ex quo opere vel actu “paracletusnominetur, vilbus eum nescio quibus spiritibus compararunt et per hoe conturbare conati sunt ecclesias Christi, ita ut dissensiones fratribus non modicas generarent. Evangelium vero tantae eum potentiae ac maiestatis ostendit, ut dicat apostolos ‘non posse capere- adhue ea, quae volebat eos docere salvator, nisi -cum advenerit spiritus sanctus’, qui se eorum animabus infundens inluminare eos possit de ratione ac fide trinitatis. Isti vero pro imperitia intellectus sui, qua non solum ipsi quod rectum est consequenter non valent exponere, sed ne his quidem quae a nobis dicuntur possunt audientiam commodare, minora de eius deitate quam dignum est sentientes, erroribus se ac deceptionibus tradiderunt, erratico magis spiritu depravati quam sancti spiritus institutionibus eruditi, secundum quod apostolus dixit: “Doctrinam spirituum daemoniorum sequentes, prohibentium nubere” “ad interitum et ruinam multorum” “et inportune se abstinere a cibis”, ut per ostentationem acrioris observantiae seducant animas innocentum, 4. Oportet ergo nos scire quia ‘paracletus’ est spiritus sanctus, docens maiora quam voce proferri possunt et, ut ita dixerim, quae ‘ineffabilia sunt- et “quae non licet homini loqui”, id est quae indicari humano sermone non possunt. Quod autem ait “non licet”, pro eo quod ‘non potest- dietum sentimus a Paulo, sicut et ibi, ubi ait: “Omnia lieent, sed non omnia expediunt; omnia licent, sed non omnia aedifieant”, Ea enim, quorum potestas nobis est, propter quod habere ea possumus, -licere- nobis dicit. ‘Paracletus’ vero quod dicitur spiritus sanctus, a consolatione dieitur enim latine consolatio appellatur); si quis namque de spiritu sancto participare meruerit, cognitis ineffabilibus sacramentis consolationem sine dubio et laetitiam cordis assumit. Cum enim rationes omnium quae fiunt, quare vel qualiter fiant, spiritu indicante cognoverit, in nullo utique conturbari eius anima poterit aut ullum sensum maeroris accipere; nec in aliquo terretur, cum verbo dei et sapientiae eius inhaerens ‘dominum lesum dicit in spiritu sancto-. Verum quoniam ‘paracleti- fecimus mentionem et pro viribus nostris qualiter de eo sentiri debeat exposuimus, dicitur autem etiam salvator noster ‘paracletus’ in epistola lohannis, cum dicit: “5i quis nostrum peccaverit, paracletum habemus ad patrem, lesum Christum iustum, et ipse est repropitiatio pro peccatis nostris”: consideremus ne forte aliud hie significet haec appellatio “paracleti- de salvatore, aliud de spiritu saneto. Videtur enim de salvatore ‘paracletus’ dici depreeator, utrumque enim significat in graeco ‘paracletus’, et “consolatoret “deprecator. Propter eum ergo qui subsequitur sermonem, quo ait quia “ipse est repropitiatio pro peccatis nostris”, magis in salvatore nomen “paraeleti- pro deprecatore intellegendum videtur; deprecari enim patrem ‘pro peccatis nostris. dicitur. De spiritu vero sancto “paracletus’ ‘consolator’ debet intellegi, pro eo quod consolationem praestat animabus, quibus aperit et revelat sensum scientiae spiritalis.

pass_b_english: Since we have already finished the first discussions, which we explained about the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit at the beginning, as the subject required, it seems right for us to return to the subject and show that God is the same creator and founder of the world and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. This is the one and the same God of the law and the prophets and the gospels. Then we must also demonstrate about Christ, that he who was shown to be the Word and wisdom of God, also how he was made man ought to be shown in what follows. It remains for us to briefly repeat what we can about the Holy Spirit. Now is the time, therefore, for us to discuss a few things about the Holy Spirit, whom our Lord and Savior in the gospel according to John named 'Paracletus' (John 14:16).

For just as the same God and the same Christ, so also the same Holy Spirit is, who was in the prophets and in the apostles. This means he was in those who before the coming of Christ believed in God, or in those who through Christ fled to God. And we have heard that some heretics dared to say there are two gods and two Christs, but we have never known anyone to preach two Holy Spirits. For how can they affirm this from the scriptures, or what difference can they give between the Holy Spirit and the Holy Spirit, if indeed some definition or description of the Holy Spirit can be found? For if we grant to Marcion or Valentinus that they can introduce differences of divinity and describe one nature as good and another as just, what will they devise or find in order to introduce a difference of the Holy Spirit? I think therefore that they can find nothing to indicate any difference. We indeed estimate that every rational creature assumes a participation of the Holy Spirit similarly to the wisdom of God and the Word of God without any difference.

We also see that the special advent of the Holy Spirit to people after the ascension of Christ into heaven is declared more than before his coming. For before, the gift of the Holy Spirit was given only to the prophets and a few, if anyone in the people deserved it. But after the coming of the Savior, it is written that 'what was spoken by the prophet Joel would be fulfilled, saying, “I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and they shall prophesy”' (Acts 2:17). This is certainly like what is said: 'All nations shall serve him' (Isaiah 66:18). By the grace of the Holy Spirit, with many others, this magnificent thing is also shown, that the things which were written in the prophets or in the law of Moses, few at that time could understand, that is, the prophets themselves and hardly anyone from the whole people could surpass the physical understanding and feel something greater, that is, what spiritual understanding could comprehend in the law or prophets. Now there are innumerable multitudes of believers, who cannot all explain the sequence of spiritual understanding in order and clearly, yet almost all are persuaded that neither circumcision should be understood physically, nor the rest of the Sabbath or the shedding of the blood of a beast, nor that answers were given to them by God about these things. Who indeed does not doubt that the power of the Holy Spirit is suggested to all.

Just as there are many understandings of Christ, who indeed is wisdom, but does not act or obtain power in all in wisdom, except in those who seek wisdom in him (nor is he called a physician to act as a physician to all, but only to those who, having understood their own sickness, flee to his mercy to obtain health), so I also think about the Holy Spirit, in whom is the nature of all gifts. For 'to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit' (1 Corinthians 12:8). And so through each one who can receive him, this is done or understood, the very Spirit by which he who has merited to participate in him stands in need. Not noticing these divisions and differences, those who hear the 'Paracletus' named in the gospel, and not considering from what work or act the 'Paracletus' is named, have compared him to some spirits I know not what, and have tried to disturb the churches of Christ, so that they have not generated small dissensions among the brothers. The gospel, however, shows such his power and majesty, that it says the apostles 'could not bear the things which the Savior wanted to teach them, unless the Holy Spirit came' (John 16:12-13), who, infusing himself into their souls, could illuminate them about the reason and faith of the Trinity. These, however, because of the ignorance of their own understanding, which not only cannot explain what is right accordingly, but also cannot give a hearing to what we say, having thought less of his divinity than is worthy, have delivered themselves to errors and deceptions, depraved more by a wandering spirit than instructed by the institutions of the Holy Spirit, according to what the apostle said: 'Following the doctrines of demons, forbidding to marry' (1 Timothy 4:1-3) 'to destruction and ruin of many, and unreasonably abstaining from foods', that by the ostentation of a stricter observance they may seduce the souls of the innocent.

Therefore, we must know that 'Paracletus' is the Holy Spirit, teaching greater things than can be uttered by voice, and, so to speak, 'ineffable things' and 'things not lawful for a man to speak', that is, things that cannot be indicated by human speech. And what is said 'not lawful', we understand to mean 'not possible' as Paul also says, as there also where he says: 'All things are lawful, but not all things are expedient; all things are lawful, but not all things edify' (1 Corinthians 6:12). For those things whose power is ours, for which we can have them, he says 'are lawful' for us. 'Paracletus', which is said to be the Holy Spirit, is called 'consolation' in Latin (for consolation is called consolation in Latin); for if anyone has merited to participate in the Holy Spirit, he certainly takes with him consolation and joy of the heart, having known the ineffable mysteries. For when he has known by the Spirit indicating the reasons of all things that are done, why and how they are done, his soul in no way can be disturbed, nor receive any sense of sorrow; nor is he terrified in any way, when clinging to the word of God and his wisdom, 'the Lord Jesus says in the Holy Spirit'. But since we have made mention of the 'Paracletus' and have explained as far as our strength how it should be thought of him, it is also said that our Savior is 'Paracletus' in the epistle of John, when he says: 'If anyone sins, we have a Paracletus with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, and he is the propitiation for our sins' (1 John 2:1). Let us consider perhaps that this name 'Paracletus' of the Savior signifies something else here, and something else of the Holy Spirit. For it seems that 'Paracletus' is said of the Savior as an intercessor, for both signify in Greek 'Paracletus', and 'consolator' and 'intercessor'. Therefore, for the one who follows the speech, where he says that 'he is the propitiation for our sins', the name 'Paracletus' of the Savior seems more to be understood as intercessor; for it is said that he intercedes for our sins. Of the Holy Spirit, 'Paracletus' must be understood as 'consolator', because he provides consolation to souls, to whom he opens and reveals the sense of spiritual knowledge.
